metadata.title: Embedded dApp Browser And CIP-30 Wallet Connector Tasks
metadata.description: Security- and standards-gated implementation graph for a wallet-scoped sandboxed dApp browser with CIP-30, CIP-8, CIP-95, CIP-103, gated CIP-104/CIP-142, software/hardware signing, ordered batch signing and submission, and soft collateral management.
metadata.importantNote: No production dApp guest may be enabled until privileged IPC sender authentication, packaged Chromium sandbox proof, full-ledger transaction context, exact byte-bound review/signing, physical hardware certification, and internal/external security reviews are complete. CIP-106 and CIP-141 are explicitly out of scope.

phases.name: Contracts, Threat Model, And Validation Spikes
phases.description: Lock normative contracts and resolve the highest-risk backend, parser, sandbox, hardware, and proposed-extension unknowns before implementation depends on them.

tasks.title: Write the hostile-renderer threat model and architecture ADR
tasks.description: Document trust boundaries, protected assets, attacker capabilities, route/origin/session invariants, approval-byte binding, the documented product limits, and release gates for the guest browser and connector.
tasks.completedNotes: Accepted hostile-renderer threat model and ADR documented in the PRD, with current-baseline evidence, threat/control traceability, architecture boundary summary, and approved planning and implementation review logs.
implementationNotes: Treat remote content as hostile even when catalogued.

Document the product limits (request CBOR size, CIP-103 batch size, page size, consent inactivity timeout) and treat within-limit availability as ordinary robustness, without weakening confidentiality or integrity controls.
Define the existing trusted renderer as privileged legacy debt, not a guest host.
acceptance: The threat model names every process, frame, IPC, backend, device, persistence, and network boundary.
The threat model documents product limits and distinguishes ordinary availability exposure from release-blocking integrity/confidentiality risks.
The ADR locks the separate BrowserWindow and main-owned broker architecture.
securityNotes: This task blocks every guest or connector implementation task.

tasks.title: Freeze CIP-30 and extension wire contracts
tasks.description: Define exact provider, base API, CIP-8, CIP-95, CIP-103, CIP-104, and CIP-142 schemas, negotiation behavior, namespace composition, typed errors, and internal Electron result envelopes.
tasks.completedNotes: Approved CIP-30 wire-contract manifest, draft-07 schemas, provenance-backed base/CIP-8/CIP-95/CIP-103 fixtures, gated CIP-104/CIP-142 dispositions, and executable contract/structured-clone evidence.
implementationNotes: Use namespaced CIP-95 getters matching Lace, Yoroi, and Cardano JS SDK despite the CIP text typo.
Keep CIP-8 out of extension negotiation.
Freeze the contract excerpts and golden fixtures used by implementation; wire contracts are pinned by fixtures, not by CIP document revisions.
Freeze the documented product limits (64 KiB request CBOR, 50-item CIP-103 batch, 100-entry page size, five-minute consent inactivity timeout) and their typed errors.
Produce CIP-8 body headers with both hashed:false and the required version:1.
Model CIP-103 mixed submission failure as a locally reconstructed rejected array.
Freeze partialSign=true with no applicable wallet key as a canonical empty witness-set success.

Freeze deprecated getCollateral as side-effect-free, nullable when current candidates are insufficient, and without a Daedalus-defined 5 ADA request maximum; document that this follows its nullable API type and ecosystem behavior where the deprecated prose conflicts.
Freeze CIP-95 DRep signData to accept the raw 28-byte DRep ID and a matching type-6 enterprise key address, while producing the raw 28-byte DRep key hash in the protected address header.
Record CIP-106 and CIP-141 as absent, not placeholder APIs.
testCases: Unknown extension request is omitted without enable failure
Unnegotiated namespace is absent
CIP-103 mixed array survives the internal IPC envelope
CIP-95 base signTx override composes deterministically
partialSign=true with no owned key returns a canonical empty witness set
getCollateral returns null without preparing collateral when current candidates are insufficient
CIP-95 DRep signData accepts raw key-hash and matching type-6 address forms and produces the same raw-hash COSE header
acceptance: Every public argument, return value, and rejection has a runtime schema.
The error matrix includes CIP-95 DeprecatedCertificate and CIP-103 rejection semantics.
PaginateError and Bech32-or-hex Address input semantics are explicit.
Deprecated getCollateral's null/no-side-effect/no-5-ADA-cap decision and its rationale are explicit.
CIP-95 DRep input normalization and protected-header bytes are locked by an interoperability vector.
Golden extracts and fixtures are recorded for every implemented standard.
No open API-shape decision remains except the explicitly gated CIP-104 encoding.

phases.name: Electron And IPC Security Foundation
phases.description: Create the auditable hostile-renderer boundary and remove guest reachability to existing privileged capabilities before exposing wallet data.

tasks.title: Harden trusted-window navigation and external URLs
tasks.description: Install trusted main navigation/popup policy before load, remove unsafe automatic popup-to-shell behavior, and require parsed approved HTTPS URLs for external opening.
tasks.completionNotes: Locked the privileged trusted window to its canonical local document, denied redirects, subframes, and popups, filtered policy-aborted recovery, made shell IPC registration explicit and process-scoped, and restricted external opening to awaited credential-free HTTPS with privacy-safe failures. Verified by focused Jest, TypeScript, production main build, and a bounded Electron 41 runtime fixture.
acceptance: Trusted renderer cannot navigate its main document or subframes to remote content; redirects and policy-aborted recovery also fail closed.
Popup handling is registered before any WebContents and never opens guest URLs automatically.
Non-HTTPS, malformed, credential-bearing, and non-string external URLs are rejected with awaited privacy-safe failures.
Import-time IPC listener side effects are removed.
securityNotes: This protects the existing Node-enabled trusted renderer from remote navigation.

tasks.title: Add trusted renderer sender and frame authentication
tasks.description: Refactor the core IPC wrappers so handlers retain Electron events, authenticate the exact trusted main WebContents/main frame, correlate responses, and register listeners before sending.
tasks.completionNotes: Added correlated listener-before-send IPC transports, exact active trusted WebContents/main-frame/document/origin authority with lifecycle cancellation, caller-frame replies, process-safe registration and hardware window rebinding, plus focused Jest and Electron 41 HTTP/file-origin evidence. Direct raw listener migration remains task-102 scope.
implementationNotes: Preserve compatibility only where concrete current callers require it.
Send responses to the authenticated caller, never a global renderer target.
Eliminate shared uncorrelated response-channel races.
acceptance: Wrong WebContents, subframe, destroyed frame, and wrong trusted origin are rejected.
Concurrent requests cannot receive each other's responses.
All wrapper tests cover sender and response authentication.

tasks.title: Audit and migrate every privileged IPC handler
tasks.description: Inventory all global privileged handlers and move them onto authenticated trusted-frame registration, including filesystem, store, TLS, logs, updates, window controls, and hardware channels.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a machine-checked 77-channel privileged IPC manifest and declaration-derived source audit, migrated close/resize controls to exact active trusted-frame wrappers, made main-originated promise ownership and current-window targeting lifecycle-safe, and proved hostile-context rejection with focused Jest, TypeScript, production builds, and a bounded Electron 41 fixture. Production guest launch remains blocked by all independent downstream gates.
implementationNotes: Create a machine-checkable inventory of channel authority across all source/main listeners, not only source/main/ipc.
Do not leave top-level listeners outside authenticated initialization.
Test known channel names from a hostile fixture.
acceptance: Every privileged channel has an explicit trusted sender/frame policy.
No guest can invoke electron-store, TLS, shell, filesystem, update, logging, or hardware operations.
The IPC architecture documentation is updated.

Never retry unsandboxed; explicit dApp-disabled wallet modes only where documented.

Every body hash and witness verifies before staging completion.
